discovery: Electromagnetic metamaterials: negative refraction, the perfect lens and transformation optics

nominees.name: Xiang Zhang
nominees.affiliation: The University of Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China

motivation: Pendry showed that sub-wavelength structured media can realise artificial magnetism and negative permittivity, predicted that a negative-index slab forms a 'perfect lens' that recovers evanescent near fields, and with Smith and coworkers founded transformation optics, the basis of invisibility cloaking. Smith made the first experimental demonstration of negative refraction in microwave metamaterials and the first cloak. Zhang took these ideas to optical frequencies with the silver superlens, which imaged below the diffraction limit, and with bulk three-dimensional optical negative-index metamaterials. Together they turned the constitutive parameters epsilon and mu from fixed material properties into quantities that can be designed. This gave optics a new set of controls that engineers now use in metasurfaces, flat lenses, hyperbolic media and structured-light devices around the world.
